presets.name: 8-bit lead
presets.desc: Classic crush: 8-bit words at 16 kHz, aliasing kept, quiet tails faded to clean instead of fizzing
presets.notes: The default: heard at once on insert. Tails Clean keeps a gain stage after it from turning the sputter into fizz

presets.name: Rack sampler 12-bit
presets.desc: Warm 12-bit grit at 26 kHz through steep anti-alias and reconstruction filters
presets.notes: The rack sampler's warmth is its filters, not its bits: 6th-order Butterworth either side of the converter

presets.name: Sampled guitar 12-bit
presets.desc: Clean guitar through a 12-bit sampler at 26 kHz: softened top, grainy tails
presets.notes: Rack Sampler 12 for a clean guitar part played as if sampled from a record

presets.name: Hot-sampled 26k
presets.desc: Drum-machine 12-bit at 26 kHz, sampled with no input filter: ringing aliases, softened images
presets.notes: Aliasing kept on purpose, a 4-pole ladder on the output: the drum-machine voicing [to tune by ear]

presets.name: Companded 8-bit
presets.desc: µ-law 8-bit words at 28 kHz: grain on loud notes, clean quiet tails, no fizz
presets.notes: Eight bits through a µ-law DAC: about 12 bits of dynamic range, the 80s drum machines' trick

presets.name: Phone line
presets.desc: Telephone voice: µ-law 8-bit at 8 kHz, band-limited 300 – 3,400 Hz
presets.notes: G.711's word and band; Clean decimation so nothing folds back into the voice

presets.name: AM radio
presets.desc: Narrow, slightly thickened voice: µ-law 8-bit at 11 kHz, 300 – 4,500 Hz
presets.notes: The old catalogue "AM radio" by intent: band-limited, a touch of DAC curve for density

presets.name: 1-bit fuzz
presets.desc: A one-bit square of the input, gated cleanly as the note decays
presets.notes: Riser at 1 bit is a square whatever the level; input +24 dB sets where the gate closes (about −18 dBFS of DI)

presets.name: Tuned crush
presets.desc: Rate locked to a multiple of the played note: the aliases land on its harmonics, in tune
presets.notes: Monophonic lines: chords hold the last rate. Best at R ≤ 8 kHz where the pitch error beats slowly

presets.name: Tuned arpeggio
presets.desc: Pitch-locked crush stepped through harmonic multiples by an eighth-note LFO
presets.notes: The LFO moves the target rate; track rounds it to whole multiples of f0: an arpeggio of crushes

presets.name: Sample-rate sweep
presets.desc: Expression-pedal sweep of the clock from 48 kHz down to 750 Hz: a glide, no zipper
presets.notes: Assign EXP to rate_shift (0 → −72 st): pitch-like travel, the fractional clock glides between every rate

presets.name: Pick-harder crush
presets.desc: The rate drops as the attack rises: harder picking crunches more
presets.notes: Envelope on the clock, negative depth: dynamics play the crush

presets.name: Synced wobble
presets.desc: Clock swept by an eighth-note sine around 8 kHz, locked to the tempo
presets.notes: Deterministic and host-synced: the same wobble on every take

presets.name: Dusty jitter
presets.desc: 10-bit sampler at 12 kHz with a wandering clock: aliases smeared into dust
presets.notes: Clock jitter turns the images and aliases into noise while the pitch stays put

presets.name: Parallel grit
presets.desc: Six-bit crush at 6 kHz blended under the dry: grit on top, the low end kept
presets.notes: The dry runs through the kernels' own response: no comb in the blend below the rate

presets.name: Old ladder DAC
presets.desc: 12-bit sampler whose ladder DAC mis-steps at mid-scale: crossover grit on quiet notes
presets.notes: R-2R bit-weight errors: quiet signals cross the wrong-sized mid-scale step [magnitude to tune by ear]

presets.name: Hit the converter
presets.desc: Input pushed 12 dB into a 10-bit converter: hard digital clipping, level compensated
presets.notes: Rate Off: the clip runs at the host rate, as a real overloaded ADC

presets.name: Clean decimate
presets.desc: Bandwidth only: 16-bit at 8 kHz through elliptic filters, no foldover
presets.notes: A brick-wall "small speaker": the Clean model removes every alias
